survey_method: every check-*.sh invoked by a workflow, run against branch and against origin/main in a clean worktree; all 43 confirmed CI-invoked with no argument differences

counts.reconciliation: 170 PASS + 21 FAIL + 1 NOT_RUN_LOCALLY = 192, from `make ci-guards-local-check` at committed HEAD on a clean tree.
counts.unit_of_count: workflow-faithful CHECKS/INVOCATIONS, not distinct shell guards. The runner takes its list from the workflow files and now includes the `make` steps CI invokes, so one guard can appear once and one make target aggregates several. 192 is invocations; guards_surveyed=189 was the earlier script-only figure.

baseline_failures_not_ours.detail: CI invokes it as `bash tools/check-openapi-compatibility.sh /tmp/openapi-old.yaml` after generating that file. Running it bare is not a valid invocation and must not be counted as a guard failure.

On origin/main it failed for one reason only: the token scan read website/app without skipping binaries and matched 'KB' inside compressed woff2 font data. On the branch it additionally failed because the guard's negation vocabulary had 'não', 'never' and 'not' but not English's determiner 'no' — and the English edition states its boundaries as 'there is no certificate authority' / 'NO CERTIFICATE AUTHORITY' / 'and no human approval'. Both fixed in e08cd68; verified green on origin/main unchanged and mutation-proven on the branch.

dominant_finding: The dominant class is STALE_GUARD_AFTER_AUTHORIZED_CHANGE, not content loss. Blocks A-E replaced literal arrays and inline strings with derived, bilingual, semantic sources; the guards grep the old syntax. Three of the fourteen non-E2 failures were triaged in depth and all three carry the same shape: the semantics survive (often strengthened, now covering both editions) while the literal the guard greps has moved.

open_findings.severity: documentation defect, corrected; scope limit recorded
open_findings.detail: The payment-operator brand list IS consumed — by the L1b scan, over contracts/ and conformance/ only. It is NOT repository-wide. Nine comments in banza-repo-guards claimed those brands 'stay blocked everywhere', which is false for the website surface, and my first analysis compounded it by reporting the constant as never read. Both corrected: the comments now say what the scan actually covers.
open_findings.consequence: a payment-operator brand on a website page is not caught by this gate. That is the gate's designed scope, now accurately documented rather than overstated.
open_findings.resolution: Repository truth established: the list IS consumed, by the L1b scan, and its ownership is exactly contracts/ and conformance/. The defect was never the code — it was nine comments asserting a broader 'blocked everywhere' property the executable code does not own. All nine are corrected to state the scan's real scope. Nothing now claims repository-wide payment-brand blocking.
open_findings.superseded_claim: my first report that the constant 'is never read'. False: it is read at the L1b scan. Kept here rather than erased, because the wrong claim is what made the surviving mutation look like dead code.
open_findings.still_true: a payment-operator brand on a website page is outside this gate's scope. That is its design, now accurately documented. Widening it would need its own change and its own survey.

open_findings.severity: design limit of the gate, recorded
open_findings.detail: the institutional-attribution allowlist admits the designated-scheme stem for a WHOLE FILE. Within an admitted page it cannot distinguish a legitimate attribution from an illegitimate claim: asserting that the scheme operates BANZA as its own payment network on the admitted English licence page does not fail the gate.
open_findings.consequence: the three admissions are correctly scoped to paths whose Portuguese counterparts are already admitted, but they do inherit this limit.
open_findings.disposition: clause-scoped admission would be a redesign of the gate; out of this PR's scope.

open_findings.severity: real coverage gap in this branch, now closed
open_findings.detail: the chrome became locale-aware, but navPrimary/footerColumns are the Portuguese realizations, so every existing assertion read one edition and the English derivation was produced by code no test ran. A withdrawn English route would have fallen back to the Portuguese path and read as a working link.
open_findings.remediation: lib/chromeLocaleDerivation.test.ts asserts both editions: same shape, own language, no silent Portuguese fallback, pathnames from the registry rather than from prefixing, locale-neutral destinations unchanged.
open_findings.mutation_evidence: English route withdrawn -> fallback + registry checks red; English URL built by prefixing the Portuguese slug -> registry check red; empty English label -> label check red. Two of the five assertions hold by construction today and are documented as such in the file rather than claimed as proven.

open_findings.found_by: adding a make target while migrating the chrome guards
open_findings.severity: CI-breaking defect introduced by this branch, now fixed
open_findings.detail: commit 7e630d9 overwrote the `## identity-check:` doc line and left its recipe orphaned, so the Makefile stopped parsing. Every `make` invocation on this branch failed at parse — including the three assurance gates identity-guard.yml runs. It went unnoticed because the runner extracted only `bash tools/check-*.sh` invocations from the workflows and ignored `run: make` steps, and because I reported the runner as wired into make without ever invoking it that way.
open_findings.remediation: Makefile repaired; the runner now extracts and executes the `make` steps too, which is why the invocation total moved from 189 to 192.
open_findings.lesson: a local model of CI that runs a convenient subset will report a clean count over a broken build. Claiming a target is wired is not the same as running it.

open_findings.severity: coverage gap, closed for the guards migrated so far
open_findings.detail: every BanzAI copy guard asserted a Portuguese literal in a module. Even before Block E2 moved the strings, that design could not see the English edition at all — so once English copy existed it was ungoverned by construction.
open_findings.remediation: the catalogues are realized once into lib/copyResolved.json and guards assert through it, which makes the English clause writable at all.
open_findings.mutation_evidence: changing ONLY the English validation-mode label now turns the guard red. Under the previous design that mutation was invisible.
open_findings.disposition: IN PROGRESS — applies to each copy guard as it is migrated

open_findings.detail: assigning from a helper that greps means a not-found result is a non-zero status, and under `set -euo pipefail` that ends the script. The guard exited 1 with its last section never printed and no failure text at all, so the inventory recorded it as failing without a reason.
open_findings.remediation: the lookups tolerate not-found and report it. A guard that dies is worse than one that fails, because there is nothing to read.
open_findings.disposition: CLOSED for three guards; the shape is `x=$(grep -c ...)` or `x=$(helper-that-greps)` under set -e

open_findings.severity: assurance defect I introduced, caught before commit
open_findings.detail: interpolating a multi-alternative phrase regex into a longer pattern without parentheses turns `PREFIX.*(A|B|C)` into `PREFIX.*A` OR `B` OR `C`. The bare last alternative then matches any line containing the phrase, so the exclusion filter silenced exactly the lines the guard exists to catch. Two mutations survived and exposed it.
open_findings.remediation: parenthesised in check-public-surface-canonical.sh and in check-open-governance.sh, which carried the same shape from the earlier English-negation fix.
open_findings.lesson: a negation/exclusion filter must be mutation-proven with a real positive claim, not only with the false positive it was written to clear.

open_findings.detail: the glossary is a table of RECORDS, not a flat id→text map, so it was flattened into the same shape (one entry per reader-visible field). Guards ask it the same way they ask every other catalogue instead of each re-parsing the term array.
